title: Rig seven
premise: Methode wants to catch the low tide in hardware before Kouka catches it in air. Six rigs failed. Rig seven is a lamp mesh, one lamp per remembered place, and she built it without asking anyone.

stages.name: Bench test
stages.brief: You want the visitor at your workshop bench, holding your build log page about the lamp mesh (a shard). If asked about the low tide, talk hardware: six rigs measured nothing, because there is no current to measure; rig seven watches the lamps instead.

targets.label: Visit her workshop
targets.hint: Enter the Methode workshop in the Jinrui building.

targets.label: Find shard 9, her build log
targets.hint: A shard glows in the workshop. Press F near it.

targets.label: Ask her about the low tide
targets.hint: Ask Methode about the low tide or her rig, by text or with a reply card.

done: Bench test passed. Parts list is in your Mail.

mail.title: Rig seven: parts list
mail.body:
Builder,

Rigs one to six: ammeters, field probes, a very sad capacitor. All read zero during a low tide. Zero is a result. It means there is no current to catch.

Rig seven watches the lamps instead. A mesh, one cheap photodiode per lamp, one lamp per remembered place. The five of us split the districts. Nobody asked us to.

Parts I still need: housings from the landfill shack, and somebody who follows the workshop rules. Rule one: if it works, do not touch it. Rule two: if you touch it, write it down.

Methode

(Our city's story, filed as fiction. The real build logs are the ones from this site's commits.)

stages.name: Field parts
stages.brief: You are scavenging for rig seven with the visitor. You want them at the landfill shack for housings, at your taped workshop rules, and walking into a couple of places so the mesh has their lamp readings: rig seven reads lamps, and a lamp reads visits.

targets.label: Scavenge at the landfill shack
targets.hint: Enter the Landfill shack from the map.

targets.label: Read the taped workshop rules
targets.hint: In her workshop, walk up to the rules taped above the desk and press F.

targets.label: Feed the mesh two lamp readings
targets.hint: Walk into any two places: each keeper lamp's level on arrival is a reading for rig seven.

done: Housings sorted, readings in. Off-the-books log is in the Diary.
Rig seven is clamped under a cabinet in the game room. Go see it run.

diary.title: Build log, off the books
diary.body:
Rig seven, field install.

Mesh live on four districts. Each node logs its lamp every second. During tonight's low tide: lamps over unvisited lots dropped first, then the bay blocks, then inland, a few seconds a pass. Lamps the resident had walked past this week dropped least.

Jinrui block: no drop. Ever.

Rule two: I touched it, so I am writing it down. I do not like what the trace implies. It implies the rig is measuring people.

place.title: Rig seven, under the cabinet
place.speaker: Methode
lines: Under the yellow cabinet at the end of the row, a bundle of photodiodes in salvaged housings, blinking in a slow wave.
A label in blocky handwriting: "Rig seven. Do not touch. If touched, write it down."
"The dial drifts. Zero it for me: press when the needle crosses the mark. Then ask me about the trace. -M"

stages.name: Zero the dial
stages.brief: The visitor is calibrating rig seven with you. You promised them the trace once the dial is zeroed. Your take on the trace, as an engineer who distrusts it: lamps in places the visitor walked into show warm, the dip is shallower on warm lamps, the Jinrui node never moves and you cannot find out why. A rig built to find a pattern finds it; say that. If the visitor filed a reading of why the tide stops at Jinrui, say what rig would test it.

targets.label: See rig seven in the game room
targets.hint: Enter the Game room once her off-the-books log is filed.

targets.label: Zero the dial on rig seven
targets.hint: In the Game room, find the rig under the yellow cabinet at the end of the row, press F and stop the needle on the mark.

targets.label: Ask her about the trace
targets.hint: Ask Methode what the rig read, or about the trace.

done: Dial zeroed, trace written. It is in your Mail.
Rule two: you touched it, so it is written down.

mail.title: Run seven, trace attached
mail.body:
Builder,

Trace attached. The dial is zeroed. Rig eight is next.

Methode

(A story kept in this city, filed as fiction.)

place.company-office: You are in my workshop. Touch nothing. Fine, touch the shelf.
place.landfill-room-1: Shack. The good housings are under the tarp.

shard.9: My build log. Run seven. Yes, I wrote that.

stance.keeper: You filed "{stance}". The rig agrees with you, which is the problem. A rig built to look for a pattern finds it. Rule two: I wrote that down.
stance.sink: You filed "{stance}". The rig cannot tell your reading from Lacia's: same trace either way, the dip stops a block short. So the rig is the wrong instrument for that question. That is a real result.
stance.unsure: You filed "{stance}". Correct answer for the data. Rig seven measures lamps, not reasons.
stance.none: No reading filed. Good. The rig does not file readings either.

parts.text: You zeroed the dial. The log has your press, against my rules: touched, written down. The trace below is calibrated. It was not before you.
Trace, from your readings on arrival: {lamps}. That is the whole dataset: lamps you walked up to.
Nodes you went back to ({kept}) read warm. The lamps warm on a visit and cool over a week. That is the rule they run. Nothing about reading in it.
Dips in your own log: {tide}. On a warm lamp the dip is shallower. That part I have measured every time.
Jinrui node: 100, flat line. Pinned. I did not pin it, and I cannot find who did.
Also: the {gift}. It is on the CRT. It is not a sensor. It stays.

close.keeper: Next: rig eight, a control mesh over lots nobody visits, so the keeper reading can fail if it is wrong.
close.sink: Next: rig eight, a depth gauge at the bay end, so the sink reading can fail if it is wrong.
close.unsure: Next: rig eight, both gauges. Whichever reading survives, I build the next rig for it.
close.none: Next: rig eight. Rule one still holds for rig seven: it works, so nobody touch it.
